Program Properties of fluids
argomenti: Density, viscosity, and other key characteristics relevant to water management
Pressure concepts and hydrostatic forces – Stevin’s law, pressure variation with depth, and hydrostatic forces on surfaces
Flow rate, velocity, and hydraulic head – continuity of flow, velocity calculation, and the concept of energy head
Bernoulli’s theorem and industrial applications – energy conservation in fluid systems and its use in industrial contexts
Water sources, demand, and monitoring with sensors – overview of supply sources, estimation of demand, and practical instrumentation
Head losses in pressurized pipe systems and simple network analysis – friction and local losses
Modelling and solving basic pipe networks
Pumping principles and pump selection – pump types, curves, efficiency, and matching pumps to system needs
Economics of pumping systems – energy costs, efficiency optimization, and life-cycle considerations
Storage of water and sizing of tanks capacity Open channel flow – principles of flow in non-pressurized systems, with applications to process units, treatment equipment and drainage
Wastewater and stormwater drainage – collection systems for industrial wastewater and stormwater in productive sites
Management of runoff from roofs and paved areas – design of detention and infiltration systems for impervious surfaces
Teaching method Teaching language: English or Italian The teaching method consists in combining short theoretical introductions with extensive problem-solving and applied exercises
Each 2-hour module begins with a focused explanation of the core concept (about 30 minutes), followed by guided calculations, design tasks, and case-based applications (about 90 minutes)
Emphasis is placed on sketching and interpreting technical representations, using realistic data from industrial and site management contexts
Perform basic calculations for pump sizing, pipeline design, and open channel flow
Estimate water demand and identify appropriate monitoring solutions with sensors
Identify the key elements of the system and the parameters needed to model it
Propose practical solutions for drainage, reuse, and sustainable water management
Up to 4 additional points may be awarded, but only if the written exam score is at least 18/30
Keeping pace with the program is strongly recommended
Submission is due within one week of the presentation of the exercise in class
